assessments.reasoning: agpl_terms [29706,30475) makes the program's specification decisive and gives the numbered later-version option, absence of a number, and proxy acceptance distinct consequences. The FSF's power to publish revisions does not itself change a version-3-only grant.

challenge.method: Compared a version-3-or-later grant, a version-3-only grant, an unnumbered AGPL grant, a program-designated proxy's public acceptance, and possession of the bare publisher document with its appendix.
challenge.results: Version 3 only supplies no later-version option under the numbered-grant rule. An authorized unnumbered AGPL grant permits any AGPL edition ever published by the FSF. If the program designates a proxy to decide future versions, the proxy's public acceptance permanently authorizes choosing that version. Possession of the license text alone does not establish even an unnumbered grant. The appendix models wording an author could adopt and supplies no evidence of adoption.

limitations: The publisher text supplies no actual program grant, proxy designation, or proxy acceptance. The rule does not establish that a later edition exists.
reasoning: Under AGPLv3 §14, an authorized program grant specifying version 3 or later gives the licensee a choice of version 3 or a later AGPL edition published by the FSF. The choice depends on what the program's grant authorizes.
